title: Znam czy wiem?
title_en: Two Polish verbs for one English "know"
note:
C1 Block 1, unit 2 — THE UNIT THAT LIFTS THE WIEM QUARANTINE (C1-SPINE O10). The fence dates to a2_directions_func, whose own note reads 'this unit NEVER mentions znam, never conjugates wiem, and never shows the infinitive', and it was re-held by b2_ze_clauses, b2_indirect_q and b2_double_neg — the last of which could not use its own headline phrase Nikt nie wie. b2_indirect_q's digest states the cost in one line: 'Dad can say I don't know where… but not Do you know where…? — which is the more useful sentence in a street.' That sentence is buildable from this node on, which is why the spine put the unit at position 2 of the level rather than in a Block 7 tidy-up.

SIX NEW FORMS, ZERO NEW ENDINGS. wiesz, wie, wiemy, wiecie, wiedzą and the infinitive wiedzieć are the whole teaching payload; wiem has been owned since a2_directions_func [68]. The endings are the -m/-sz set the learner has had since A1 on mieć, and slide 1 is that parallel run down the page (mam/masz/ma/mamy/macie against wiem/wiesz/wie/wiemy/wiecie) with wiedzą named as the ONE place the parallel breaks — mają would predict a form that does not exist. Note mamy is used here in the job AGENTS' own homograph table assigns it, the verb 'we have', never as a Genitive of mama.

THE SPLIT COSTS ONE PARADIGM, NOT TWO, and that was verified rather than assumed: check_new.py reports znać / znam / znasz / zna / znamy / znacie / znają ALL TAUGHT since a1_present [15], so the wiedzieć-vs-znać contrast is a selection fact laid over a paradigm the learner has had for 150 nodes. This is the one place the unit carries two things at once, and it is defensible on exactly that ground — the second thing is not new material. The test given is syntactic, not semantic, because a syntactic test is one the learner can actually apply: if what follows could stand alone as a sentence, it is wiedzieć; if it is a person, a place or a thing you could point at, it is znać.

STAGE DIVISION OF LABOUR, deliberate. Pisanie drills the PARADIGM (six single forms — the AGENTS 'a single form for conjugation' contract, the b2_powinien idiom) plus three short selection items on the znać side, so no answer repeats under the engine's own norm(). Kontrola drills the SELECTION, since choosing between two verbs is a discrimination and that is what a quiz is for. Użycie is where the two meet in real sentences.

ACCUSATIVE OBJECTS ARE POOL-LIMITED AND THAT SHAPED THE UNIT: tę is verified NEW, so no feminine demonstrative object exists at this position, and kobietę, kolegę and lekarza are all NEW too. Every znać object here is therefore a masculine inanimate (adres, ten sklep, ten hotel, ten numer — Accusative identical to Nominative), a neuter (to miasto), or the honest masculine-animate Acc≡Gen case AGENTS names. No new noun form rides in.

DISTRACTORS are taught words in the wrong slot, never fabricated non-words: Wiem adres, Znam, gdzie jest bank, Dzieci wie, Oni zna. Slide 4 shows the two commonest wrong sentences EXPLICITLY under a 'Polish does not say' column rather than leaving them to be discovered, on the b2_copular_future precedent that printed będę być and said outright it is not Polish.

FENCED: wiedza the noun (so wiedzą is only ever the verb here); the past of wiedzieć (wiedziałem — verified NEW, and a second system in a unit that already carries a paradigm and a split); umieć, which is the third English 'know how to' and is owned only as umiem/umiesz from a vocab leaf, left alone rather than dragged into a two-way contrast; and je, the 3sg of jeść, which would have made the mieć/wiedzieć parallel prettier and is verified NEW and fenced to c1_pron_je.

intro.title: The verb behind wiem
intro.title_pl: wiem · wiesz · wie · wiemy · wiecie · wiedzą
intro.body: Nie wiem has been a street phrase since A2, and Wiem, że… has been available since B2 — but only ever in the first person. The verb is wiedzieć, and it does not conjugate like anything else you have learned by rule. It takes the -m / -sz endings you have had since A1 on mieć.

examples.en: Mum knows where the shop is.
We know that Dad is at work.

intro.title: wiedzą is the one place the parallel breaks
intro.body: Five rows of that table run in step. The sixth does not: mieć has mają, and wiedzieć has wiedzą. There is no rule to derive it from — it is the one form of this verb to learn as a word. Everything else follows mam.

examples.en: The children know where Mum is.

intro.title: One English word, two Polish verbs
intro.body: English says know for both. Polish splits them, and the split is about what comes after the verb rather than about meaning, which makes it a test you can apply. wiedzieć takes a whole clause — a że, a gdzie, a czy. znać takes a noun: a person, a place, a thing you could point at. znać is not new; you have had znam since A1.

rows: I know where the pharmacy is.
I know that Dad is at work.

intro.title: The question you have not been able to ask
intro.body: Nie wiem, gdzie jest apteka has been in your mouth since A2. The far more useful sentence is the same one asked of somebody else, and until now there was no form to ask it with. wiesz is that form, and it works with every question word you already put after nie wiem.

rows: Nie wiem, kiedy sklep jest otwarty.
Czy wiesz, kiedy sklep jest otwarty?

examples.en: Do you know where the bank is?
Do you know what time it is?

intro.title: What each verb refuses
intro.title_pl: Znam adres. · Wiem, gdzie jest bank.
intro.body: Neither verb covers the other's job, and putting the wrong one in is the predictable mistake for an English speaker, because English hides the difference. Both wrong sentences below are built from words you own; they are simply not what Polish says.

examples.en: I know the address, but I don't know where the hotel is.
examples.pl: Znam adres, ale nie wiem, gdzie jest hotel.

match.en: I know where the pharmacy is.
Do you know where the bank is?
Mum knows where the shop is.

Do you (plural) know when the shop is open?
match.pl: Czy wiecie, kiedy sklep jest otwarty?

match.en: The children know where Mum is.

quiz.prompt: Do you know where the bank is? (one person) →
quiz.explain: A whole clause follows, so the verb has to be wiedzieć — znać cannot take one. One person you are talking to, so wiesz.
adres is a thing, not a clause, so it takes znać. Wiem adres is the mistake English invites, because English uses one verb for both.

quiz.prompt: Mum knows where the shop is. →
quiz.explain: One person being talked about — the on / ona slot, so wie. And a clause follows, so it cannot be zna.

quiz.prompt: The children know where Mum is. →
quiz.explain: More than one, being talked about: wiedzą. This is the form with no parallel in mieć — mają would predict something else.

quiz.prompt: Do you know this hotel? (one person) →
quiz.explain: A hotel is a place you could point at, so znać. znacie would be right if you were asking more than one person.

quiz.prompt: ___, gdzie jest apteka? (do you know — one person)
quiz.explain: The sentence you have wanted since A2. Wiem would say it about yourself; Znasz cannot take the clause at all.
wy → wiecie, exactly as wy → macie.
my → wiemy, exactly as my → mamy.
A city is a place — znać. And tata is one person being talked about, so zna, not znają.

quiz.prompt: I don't know how much it costs. →
quiz.explain: The A2 street phrase, unchanged. What is new is that the other three forms now exist and mean somebody else.

quiz.prompt: Do you know when the shop is open? (more than one person) →
choices: Czy wiecie, kiedy sklep jest otwarty?
Czy wiemy, kiedy sklep jest otwarty?
Czy wiedzą, kiedy sklep jest otwarty?
Czy znacie, kiedy sklep jest otwarty?
quiz.answer: Czy wiecie, kiedy sklep jest otwarty?
quiz.explain: Asking more than one person: wiecie. wiedzą would be asking about them rather than asking them.
The verb has to be znać because adres is a thing — and then the ending follows oni: znają.

type_items.explain: The -sz ending you already put on masz.
Bare stem, no ending at all — the same shape as ma.

type_items.prompt_en: you know (a fact — more than one person) →

type_items.explain: The one form with no parallel in mieć. mają would predict something else; this is a word to learn rather than a form to build.

type_items.prompt_en: Do you know this hotel? (one person)
type_items.explain: A hotel is a thing, so the verb is znać — and the person you are asking is one, so znasz.
type_items.note: Pisanie hard cap (James 2026-08-06). Composed, 4 words. Blank on the SELECTION, which is this unit's second teaching point: the choice of znać over wiedzieć, in the person the question needs.
